# Introduction

This project seeks to visualize food access across higher education institutions in Erie County, NY by assessing their overall food environment. Using the five dimensions of food access, also known as the ***5A's of food environment***, this interactive R project will provide an overview of

- _availability and accessibility_, which captures the geographical ease with which individuals can access food retailers;
- _affordability_, which captures objective and subjective measures of cost; and
- _acceptability and accommodation_, which reflect perceptions and cultural norms related to the food environment in Erie County and the Western New York (WNY) region.

By creating an interactive web page for spatial analysis, this project utilizes the user-friendly R-language to present the current food landscape through the lens of students in higher education, an often-overlooked demographic in local health and nutrition policies.

## Why understand food access for college students? 

[As of 2024, 12.5% of Erie County residents face food insecurity, with approximately 63% of those residents falling below the threshold to be SNAP-eligible. An increase of 1.1% since 2019, the county is experiencing an annual food budget shortfall of approximately $92 million, leading to a significant increase in food prices and taxes on food and beverages](https://map.feedingamerica.org/county/2019/overall/new-york/county/erie). Research indicates that although food insecurity across all demographics is an increasing concern and must be understood at an individual level, broad categorizations of these groups increase invisibility of already vulnerable populations. [For instance, in 2020, 19 – 56% of students reported being food insecure on college campuses, four times more than the national average, and their prevalence depending on campus location and related factors](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph20105884). 

Demographic selection is not the only variable that lacks comprehensive analysis. [Studies show that existing research trends surrounding food and nutritional access often overlook all five dimensions from context-specific methodologies](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jneb.2022.02.017). This dearth in frame of reference, when handpicking only few aspects of the food environment as the central theses, leads to further disparities in how we evaluate the perceptions of healthy, nutritious food available to individuals in a community.

## Whose food access are we looking at?

```{r}
#| label: institution-map
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(leaflet)

input_path <- file.path(
  "data",
  "processed",
  "eriecounty_institutions_geocoded.csv"
)

if (!file.exists(input_path)) {
  stop(
    "Geocoded institution CSV not found. ",
    "Run geocode_institutions.r first.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

institutions <- read.csv(
  input_path,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)

required_columns <- c(
  "institution",
  "address",
  "latitude",
  "longitude"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(institutions)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "Missing required columns: ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

institutions$latitude <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(
    trimws(as.character(institutions$latitude))
  )
)

institutions$longitude <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(
    trimws(as.character(institutions$longitude))
  )
)

valid_coordinates <- with(
  institutions,
  is.finite(latitude) &
    is.finite(longitude) &
    latitude >= -90 &
    latitude <= 90 &
    longitude >= -180 &
    longitude <= 180
)

institutions <- institutions[
  valid_coordinates,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

if (nrow(institutions) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "No usable coordinates found. ",
    "Run geocode_institutions.r first.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

leaflet(institutions) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    label = ~institution,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<strong>",
      htmltools::htmlEscape(institution),
      "</strong><br>",
      htmltools::htmlEscape(address)
    )
  ) |>
  fitBounds(
    lng1 = max(-180, min(institutions$longitude) - 0.01),
    lat1 = max(-90, min(institutions$latitude) - 0.01),
    lng2 = min(180, max(institutions$longitude) + 0.01),
    lat2 = min(90, max(institutions$latitude) + 0.01)
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Explore the food access dashboard" appearance="default"}
[Click here to learn more about how Erie County's higher institutions perform within the five dimensions of the food environment!](dashboard.qmd)

Please note that the institution list is not exhaustive and may contain incomplete/missing data.

Data discrepancy example: SUNY Buffalo has three campuses across Erie County county, with numerous smaller institutions that partially functions as an educational organization. However, NYSED data only highlights the main North campus as the reference point for displaying institutional information. 

See [Next Steps](about.qmd#future-research-author-note) for further insights on future methodological and data processing steps for this project.
:::
